text:
nora: FYI Acme support ticket — their indexing pipeline is getting intermittent rejects from our vecdb. They say ~12% of batches fail with "vector dimension mismatch" after a model swap yesterday.

matt: Ugh. Do we know which model they were on and what changed?

nora: They were on redwood/semantic-embed-vX (hosted). Ops log shows embeddings mostly 1536 but some responses returned 1024 in the same minute. Customer ingest job batches 64 vectors; indexer rejects whole batch when dims differ.

alice: Can we get a concrete repro? Ask them for a small failing payload + request ids. Also check if our autoscaling spilled requests to an older model variant.

kyle: Quick check: last deploy rolled a quantized variant for latency. That variant uses 1024 output dim (legacy). Routing policy should've pinned to vX but fallback path to vX-legacy exists. I can grep routing logs.

ops-bot: [alert] 1745678950 deploy-bot: model rollout redwood/semantic-embed-vX -> 100% completed at 1745678920. Minor canary at 1745678860.

matt: If their job got split across hosts during the rollout, some requests could have hit the old variant. That explains mixed dims in a single batch window.

nora: Customer provided this error snippet from their indexer: ```ERROR: Insert failed: expected vector dim=1536 got dim=1024 for id=acme-obj-1234```. They also attached a chunk of the request payload with X-Request-Id headers.

alice: Ask them to send us the exact X-Request-Id for a failing batch. We can correlate to our request logs and model variant served. Also ask for a small repro (2-3 documents) and the SDK version.

kyle: Found a few request traces around 1745678915 that were routed to redwood/semantic-embed-vX-legacy. Looks like the routing table had a transient entry during the canary rollout window. I'll attach traces in support ticket.

matt: Two vectors in the same batch having different dims points to either: 1) client batch accidentally mixing older vectors (unlikely) or 2) service-routing mixing model versions for requests within the same logical batch (more likely given timeframe).

nora: Customer also flagged billing: they were billed at token rates for some of the failed requests. They want credit for failed inserts.

alice: Support action items: 1) Correlate failing X-Request-Ids to model variant and host. 2) Offer pro-rated credit for failed inserts and waive billing for those request IDs. 3) Provide short-term mitigation instructions so their indexer can validate dims client-side before sending.

kyle: Mitigation suggestion to customer (quick): validate embedding dim.length == 1536 before calling vecdb. Example snippet: ```python
if len(embedding) != 1536:
    retry_embedding_call()
``` This avoids full-batch rejects.

nora: For internal fix: disable fallback to legacy quantized variant during rollouts for endpoints that changed embedding dims, or enforce model-compatibility checks in routing.

matt: Also need a postmortem checklist: - confirm rollout gating rules, - add canary traffic shaping to avoid cross-batch variance, - add alert if mixed-dim responses seen from an endpoint.

support-bot: Created ticket #SUP-4921 (customer: Acme) and added billing_hold label.

alice: I've drafted a customer message: "We're sorry — we found a transient routing to a legacy variant during the rollout which produced 1024-dim embeddings. We'll credit failed inserts and prevent this by blocking cross-variant routing for endpoints with embedding shape changes. Can you share the failing X-Request-Ids so we can refund those calls?" Thoughts?

nora: Sounds good. Add ETA: temporary mitigation today, rollback safelist for legacy variants within 24h, longer-term routing fix in next sprint.

kyle: I'll open an eng runtime PR to make dim metadata part of routing keys. That will prevent serving mismatched-model outputs into the same logical endpoint.

matt: For now, ops: mark the legacy variant as not-eligible for fallback for endpoints where embed_dim != expected. Then we can re-run the customer's failed batches after backfill.

ops-bot: [action] 1745679060 ops: marked variant redwood/semantic-embed-vX-legacy as no-fallback for tenant-scoped endpoints.

nora: Customer replied with 3 failing X-Request-Ids. I'm going to attach correlation info and the credit proposal. Will schedule short call if they want a walkthrough of mitigation.

alice: Nice. After we confirm credits, propose a backfill plan: 1) re-embed affected documents with the correct model variant using a batch job, 2) run indexer in idempotent upsert mode, 3) monitor rejects and billing. Provide their engineers a backfill script example.

kyle: Backfill script example (send small rate-limited job): ```bash
# fetch failing ids from ticket
for id in $(cat failed_ids.txt); do
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPRO_KEY" -d "{...}" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings | jq .embedding > out.json
  # upsert into vecdb
done
```

matt: OK team — let's prioritize: Alice will send the customer note and credit plan; Kyle will open the runtime PR; Ops has already blocked fallback. Keep me looped on the backfill progress.

nora: Will update ticket and close thread after customer confirmation. :thumbsup:
